results.one_line: The duty is real: under the 2024 security law (LOVSP), a lapsed policy or permit means permanent permit cancellation, and 2026 brought inspection waves and closures. But a tracker of permit, policy, guard-retraining and arms expiries serves only about 700-1,130 low-margin firms, the state already holds most of the data in SICOSEP, and the insurance supervisor reports policy status to the ministry quarterly.
results.buyers: About 700-1,130 private security companies. At least 1,130 registered firms and more than 90,000 guards (Primicias, Apr 2026, armed-forces inspection plan). 541 firms held permits in 2022 (Interior ministry via El Universo). The gob.ec MDI-61 renewal page shows 364 renewal "atenciones" in Sep 2025-Aug 2026; on a 2-year cycle that suggests ~730 live permits (my inference). 178 firms are on SERCOP's public-sector catalogue.
results.price: Plausible USD 40-150/month per firm, tiered by guard count (unverified). Today firms pay USD 50 per renewal (USD 200 per year late) plus ad hoc lawyer fees (no prices found). International guard-tour tools start around USD 20/month (OfficerReports). No local compliance tool price exists.
results.top_competitor: SICOSEP, the Interior ministry's free system for permit filing and the registry of guards, arms, posts and policies. Next closest is Secusoft (Dutch, with Ecuador roots), which does rostering and guard tours but no compliance expiries.
results.killer: None decisive. Biggest risk: the state already holds the data (SICOSEP, the SincoAr arms app, the quarterly policy feed to the ministry under the 10th general provision) and could add expiry alerts. Add a tiny low-margin market and possible art. 43 accreditation for software sold to security firms.

results.one_line: The SENACLAFT anti-money-laundering (PLAFT) duty for non-financial subjects is real and widened in 2026, but two Uruguayan SaaS tools already sell the exact workflow (Cumplo360, HADA) into a small, lightly enforced market.
results.buyers: 12,660 non-financial subjects registered with SENACLAFT in May 2019. These include 2,058 estate agencies, 949 accountants, 391 auctioneers, 165 corporate-service providers and 133 lawyers (about 3,700 in the core segment), plus 7,368 notaries and 1,568 free-zone entities. Source: GAFILAT Mutual Evaluation of Uruguay 2020, Table 22, https://biblioteca.gafilat.org/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/IEM-Uruguay.pdf. No 2026 count was found.
results.price: HADA has a prepaid plan from US$10 plus tax; its annual Lite and Full plans have no public price. Cumplo360 sells scalable plans with no public price, and Crowe sells a done-for-you due-diligence service, also unpriced. A plausible newcomer price is US$15-40 per month or US$10-30 per client file (unverified). Fines run from UI 1,000 to UI 20M, but there were only 14 fines across all non-financial sectors in 2023.
results.top_competitor: Cumplo360 by Devsys (Montevideo). It claims 350+ clients and alignment with SENACLAFT and BCU, and has real estate, notary and accountant users. HADA by GNS Software is close behind, with a risk matrix, simplified/normal/intensified due diligence and suspicious-activity report generation from US$10 prepaid.
results.killer: Established local SaaS products (Cumplo360, HADA) already cover the risk matrix, due diligence, screening and suspicious-activity reports for Uruguayan non-financial subjects. The core market is about 3,700 firms, enforcement is light (50 sanctions in 2023) and SENACLAFT publishes free forms, so a third entrant has little room.

results.one_line: The SEPRELAD duties for jewellers and pawnshops are real, but only about 108 jewellers and 23 pawnshops are active in SIRO, neither sector has ever been sanctioned, and filing is done in the free state portal, so the niche is too small to sell into.
results.buyers: In 2025, 108 jewellers and 23 pawnshops paid the SIRO canon. New registrations since 2022 total 192 jewellers and 32 pawnshops. The wider pool of firms SEPRELAD supervises directly adds 845 vehicle dealers and 1,451 real-estate firms paying the canon in 2025, out of about 6,065 directly supervised subjects in total. Sources: the SEPRELAD SIRO public statistics module (seprelad.gov.py/siro/estadisticaExterna/estadistica.xhtml, queried 9 Oct 2026) and the SEPRELAD Memoria 2024.
results.price: Today buyers pay only the SIRO canon of about Gs 217k-334k a year (about US$30-45). Consultant prices for a manual and risk matrix were not found; my estimate is US$200-650 one-off (unverified). A plausible SaaS price is US$10-20 a month, which gives a niche ceiling of about US$23k a year even if all 130 firms bought.
results.top_competitor: The free SEPRELAD SIRO portal, which handles registration, ROS and negative-report filing, the annual form and fees, together with SEPRELAD's free training events. Registered specialist external auditors (64 admitted in 2024) and law firms also offer manuals and audits.
results.killer: The market is too small and nothing pushes it to buy. There are about 130 active jewellers and pawnshops in total, SEPRELAD recorded zero sanctions on either sector in 2022-2026, and filing already happens in the free SIRO portal. Enforcement falls on real estate and vehicle dealers instead: 1,692 warning notes in 2024.

results.one_line: Uganda's OSH (Amendment) Act No. 20 of 2025 now covers every workplace and adds duties: a committee, a safety officer, a health surveillance plan, incident notification and annual audits. But registration goes through the free OSHMIS portal and enforcement is very thin, so the opening is a modest compliance-pack service for about 33,000 formal employers.
results.buyers: In principle every workplace since July 2025 (likely several hundred thousand; the UBOS COBE 2019/20 totals could not be opened). Realistic paying base: about 33,200 active NSSF employers out of 113,200 registered and 850,000+ URSB entities (Monitor commentary, 2025). The number of registered workplaces is not published.
results.price: No published consultant or registration prices were found. The official fee is unknown. In 2013 total registration and plant-exam fee revenue was only about UGX 100m a year. Estimate (unverified): UGX 300k-1.5m (USD 80-400) a year for a done-for-you pack. One known offence carries a fine of up to 1,000 currency points (about UGX 20m), per a secondary source.
results.top_competitor: The free MGLSD OSHMIS portal (oshmis.mglsd.go.ug), which handles workplace registration. Other rivals: local OSH consultancies and law firms (Kashari Consults, KAA, KTA) and generic HSE apps (DNV Synergi, HSE Masters' HSEQ App). No commercial Ugandan OSH SaaS was found.
results.killer: None confirmed. The biggest risk is weak enforcement: about 400 inspections a year in 2013, a 70%-staffed department in 2025, and fewer than half of workplaces inspected (EPRC 2026). Together with the free OSHMIS portal, this means little pressure to pay. Implementing regulations with deadlines are still pending.

results.one_line: Law 263-VIII (Feb 2026) creates a real duty for Kazakh security firms: a quarterly 13-block email report to the MVD and notices within 5 days. But it is one template a quarter and I found no fine for missing it, so a tool built only for that report will not sell; a wider guard-company back office is a different, harder business.
results.buyers: About 4,463 private security organisations were registered at 1 January 2026, with over 97,000 guards (kapital.kz, 29.01.2026). Other counts are 5,129 (inbusiness.kz) and about 4,200 operating with 800 suspended (24.kz, April 2025). That leaves roughly 3,000 to 3,700 active firms, plus alarm installers and training centres (no count found).
results.price: Firms pay nothing today: the report is filled in-house in Excel or Word and emailed. A plausible price is 5,000 to 15,000 tenge a month (USD 10 to 30) for a full back office, in line with GuardsPro (from USD 10 a month) and QR-Patrol (from USD 2.46 per guard a month). A report-only tool might earn 2,000 to 3,000 tenge a month (estimate). The fines that do exist (Administrative Code Art. 470) are 40, 80 or 100 MRP, about 173,000 to 432,500 tenge, but they do not cover missed reports.
results.top_competitor: Excel plus email, done in-house. No Kazakh vendor or 1C configuration was found. A possible MVD system, "E-kuzet", is unverified. International guard software (GuardsPro, QR-Patrol, TrackTik) and Russia's anolla.com do not cover Kazakh MVD reporting.
results.killer: Firms have little reason to pay. The duty is one quarterly email template, and Administrative Code Art. 470 has no fine for failing to file the report or the 5-day notice. On top of that, the MVD could move reporting to its own portal (E-kuzet, unverified).

results.one_line: Resolution 315 (in force 22 June 2026) does create recurring valve, vessel, metrology and staff-attestation duties for about 6,200 fuel and gas sites, and these are enforced through suspensions. But the same resolution orders the state to build online tracking of those same deadlines. Meanwhile the core small-owner segment, the CNG stations, is shrinking under gas shortages and the real cost is new equipment, not paperwork.
results.buyers: 6,196 fuel/gas sites inventoried (AZS, AGZS, AGNKS, cylinder points) and 1,553 AGNKS registered in U-Gas (lex.uz/ru/docs/8280849; gov.uz/ru/cirns/news/view/196046). The number of distinct owners and the private/chain/state split were not found (unverified).
results.price: Own estimate: about 150k-400k soums (USD 12-30) per site per month, or a one-off readiness audit of a few million soums. No public prices were found for expert organisations, attestation centres or accountants. Fire fines on officials are 3-10 BRV (about 1.2-4.1m soums). The main cost of breaking the rules is suspension.
results.top_competitor: State systems: U-Gas (Uzinfocom), with metrology deadlines in TRIS, online equipment-test monitoring ordered under Res. 315 point 4b, Licence-system staff-certification tracking, and Res. 325 industrial-safety e-services. No private tracker was found. 1C:KA AZS covers accounting only.
results.killer: The state is digitising the same deadlines for free (Res. 315 points 4b, 7 and 12, U-Gas, Res. 325). It is selling into a small, squeezed buyer base: methane stations closed to private cars in winter 2026, new CNG stations discouraged, and LPG stations phased down since 2017.

results.one_line: Croatian employers of third-country workers face a rule set that is real, changing and enforced. Fines run 500-15,000 EUR per breach, and labour inspectors found 961 illegally working foreigners and shut down 263 employers for 30 days in 2025. No local tool tracks permit expiry, notices, the new police-area limit or the housing rules, but the product is thin, and agencies and generic HR tools sit close by.
results.buyers: The number of employers is not published. MUP issued 94,113 permits in H1 2026 (37,230 new, 36,601 renewals, 20,282 seasonal; tourism 39,054, construction 23,708) and 170,723 in 2025. I estimate 10,000-25,000 employers (unverified). Sources: mup.gov.hr June 2026 statistics, moj-posao.net.
results.price: Suggested 29-99 EUR per month per employer, or 2-4 EUR per worker per month; agencies 150-400 EUR per month (estimate). Today employers pay state fees of 74.32 EUR plus 31.85 EUR per permit, and 125 EUR for a webinar on the rules (Informator). Moja Firma charges 29.99-59.99 EUR per month for adjacent HR records. Agency and lawyer fees were not found.
results.top_competitor: Moja Firma (mojafirma.hr). It is a Croatian HR and time-records SaaS at 29.99-59.99 EUR per month that publishes a foreign-worker guide but has no permit tracking. The other alternatives are employment agencies and lawyers doing the filing, plus the HZZ and MUP filing apps, which do not track deadlines.
results.killer: None found. The biggest risk is a thin product (reminders plus checklists) that generic HR tools or agencies can copy, plus the state JEER real-time work-records system linked to MUP permits.

results.one_line: Panama's SSNF supervises about 12,800 non-financial obliged subjects (62% lawyers and accountants) and actively issues questionnaires, inspects and sanctions; the free SSNF portal handles every filing, so a product must sell the internal programme (client risk matrix, annual review, training log, 15-day questionnaire readiness) to price-sensitive small offices, against 35+ registered compliance firms and a few local screening tools.
results.buyers: 12,802 SONF registered at 31 Dec 2025, of which 7,915 (62%) are in the professional sector (lawyers, law firms, accountants), 2,415 in free zones and 2,130 in real estate and construction (SSNF indicator dashboard, monitoreo.antai.gob.pa). Most are small offices (unverified for 2025).
results.price: Estimated US$30-80 a month per small office for software (unverified). No published prices were found for the 35+ SSNF-registered compliance firms or for InteliCumplo, PEP Check or AgileCheck. Firms already pay for the independent review the SSNF guide requires every 2 years. Reported fines start at $1,000-$5,000.
results.top_competitor: The free SSNF en línea portal covers registration and all filings, including the questionnaire and extra-situ forms. For the internal programme, the alternatives are the 35+ SSNF-registered compliance firms (APEC association) and local tools: InteliCumplo (APC Intelidat), PEP Check (sof-IA) and AgileCheck Express.
results.killer: No outright killer. The biggest risk is a thin market. The free state portal does all the filings, and the self-assessment questionnaire comes only on SSNF request (15 business days to answer), not on a fixed calendar. The buyers are about 7,900 price-sensitive small professionals, many of whom drop regulated work rather than pay for compliance. Established compliance firms already serve this gap.
